title: NewLocationPanel uses apiPost which returns void -- onSaved receives undefined GUID
detail: Line 170: `const res = await apiPost('/dcfg_properties', {...});` followed by line 182: `onSaved(res?.dcfg_propertyid ?? '');`. apiPost is a void function (see CR-2026-04-09-0210), so `res` is always undefined and `res?.dcfg_propertyid` is always undefined. The user sees the toast 'Location created successfully' and the panel closes, but `onSaved('')` navigates to `/locations/` (empty ID) which loads the Locations list again rather than the new location detail. The record IS created in Dataverse, so there's no data loss, but the post-create navigation is broken. Should use apiPostReturnId to get the new record GUID.
evidence: Locations.jsx:170 `const res = await apiPost(...)`, :182 `onSaved(res?.dcfg_propertyid ?? '')`. portalApi.js apiPost returns void per CR-2026-04-09-0210.
recommendedFix: Change `apiPost` to `apiPostReturnId` on line 170: `const newId = await apiPostReturnId('/dcfg_properties', {...});` then `onSaved(newId);`.

title: Locations fetches ALL active dcfg_location_documents on every mount just for alert badges
detail: Line 40: `apiGet('/dcfg_location_documents?$filter=dcfg_is_active eq true&$select=_dcfg_property_id_value,dcfg_alert_status')` fetches every active compliance document in the system to build a worst-alert-status map per location. With ~150 locations having ~5 docs each, this is ~750 rows transferred on every Locations list mount. If the document count grows (e.g. 500 locations with 10 docs = 5000), this becomes a noticeable payload. No $top cap, no server-side aggregation.
recommendedFix: Add a reasonable $top (e.g. 5000) with a console.warn when hit. Longer term, compute worst-alert-status server-side via a calculated column or a scheduled flow that stamps the worst status on the property record.

title: New Location button has no role-guard -- any authenticated user can create locations
detail: Line 76: `<button data-testid="loc-btn-new" onClick={() => setShowNewPanel(true)} ...>+ New Location</button>` is rendered unconditionally. The component destructures `isAdmin, isManager` from usePortalUser but never uses them to gate the create button. A Viewer-role user can open the panel and create a location record. Per JS-06/C-06 (actions the user cannot perform are REMOVED FROM THE DOM), the create button should be hidden for non-admin/non-manager users.
evidence: Locations.jsx:21 destructures isAdmin/isManager, :76 button rendered unconditionally.
recommendedFix: Wrap the button render in `{(isAdmin || isManager) && <button ...>+ New Location</button>}`. Same guard on line 145 `showNewPanel` conditional.

title: Customer filter dropdown and search input lack aria-label attributes
detail: Line 89: `<select data-testid="loc-filter-customer" ...>` has no aria-label or associated <label>. Line 82: search input has placeholder text but no aria-label. Screen readers will not identify the purpose of these controls.
evidence: Locations.jsx:89 select, :82 input -- no aria-label attributes.
recommendedFix: Add `aria-label="Filter by customer"` to the select on line 89. Add `aria-label="Search locations"` to the search input on line 82.

title: ComplianceDocs receives hardcoded isManager={true} -- all users can upload and deactivate documents
detail: Line 252: `<ComplianceDocs ... isManager={true} .../>`. The `isManager` prop controls whether the Upload Document button and the Mark Inactive buttons are rendered. By hardcoding `true`, every user (including Viewers) sees and can use these actions. The component destructures `isAdmin, isManager` from usePortalUser at line 119 but passes a hardcoded true instead of the actual role check.
evidence: LocationDetail.jsx:252 `isManager={true}`, :119 destructures actual isAdmin/isManager but does not pass them.

title: Secondary fetches in reload() silently return empty data on failure -- no user notification
detail: Line 133-161: `reload()` uses Promise.allSettled for detail/docs/appliances. Rejected results silently fall to null/empty. A user can land on a location page where property info loads fine but docs/appliances return empty arrays due to a permissions error, and the user sees 'No compliance documents found' instead of an error message.
evidence: LocationDetail.jsx:138 Promise.allSettled, :143-145 fulfilled checks -- rejected results set to null silently.
recommendedFix: Add a toast notification for each rejected secondary fetch: `if (detRes.status === 'rejected') toast.show('warn', 'Could not load facility details');`.

title: handleDeactivate in AppliancesTab has no try/catch -- unhandled rejection on failure
detail: Lines 530-533: `async function handleDeactivate(id) { await apiPatch(...); if (onReload) onReload(); }`. No try/catch block. If the PATCH fails, the error is unhandled.
recommendedFix: Wrap in try/catch with toast error surface.

title: handleMarkInactive has no try/catch and no await on reload()
detail: Lines 186-189: No try/catch, so a PATCH failure is an unhandled rejection. Also `reload()` is called without await.
evidence: LocationDetail.jsx:186-189 -- no error handling on mark-inactive.
recommendedFix: Add try/catch with toast error surface, and await the reload call.

title: AppliancesTab appliance type fetch has bare .catch(() => {}) -- silent failure
detail: Line 509: `.catch(() => {});` -- if appliance types query fails, types dropdown is empty with no error message.

title: fetchWorkOrders N+1 location resolution -- up to 50 sequential API calls on first load
detail: Lines 204-216: for every unresolved location ID, a separate apiGet fires. With 50 unique locations this is 50 sequential calls. The locationMapRef cache mitigates repeat polls, but first load can be very slow.
evidence: Operations.jsx:200-216 -- Promise.all of individual location lookups.
recommendedFix: Batch unresolved location IDs into a single OData `$filter=dcfg_upkeep_location_id in (...)` query.

title: Work order location resolution has bare catch {} -- individual failures invisible
detail: Line 210: `} catch {}` in the per-location resolution loop. No diagnostic output for failed location lookups.
recommendedFix: Add console.warn with the failed locId.

title: CompliancePanel queries have no $select -- returns all columns from rules and checks tables
detail: Lines 146 and 158: both apiGet calls on complianceRules and complianceChecks have no $select clause. If these tables are on explicit field lists, bare GETs will 403.
recommendedFix: Add $select to both queries listing only the columns read by the component.

title: Directory data load has bare catch -- no error surface for users
detail: Line 82: `.catch(function() { setLoading(false); });` -- if vendors or customers query fails, loading stops but no error message is shown. User sees empty directory with 'No contacts found.'
evidence: Directory.jsx:82 -- bare catch with no error state.
recommendedFix: Add error state and render error message above results list.

title: MapView popup HTML injects raw location/customer names without escaping -- XSS vector
detail: Lines 136-142: Leaflet popup content is built via template literal HTML with unescaped Dataverse values. If a location name contains HTML tags, they will be rendered/executed.
evidence: MapView.jsx:134-143 -- template literal popup with unescaped user data.
recommendedFix: Create popup content via DOM API instead of HTML string, or add an escapeHtml utility.

title: MapView toast missing from useEffect dependency array
detail: Line 97: useEffect uses toast in body but deps array is `[]`. Unlikely to cause bugs since useToast returns a stable ref, but is a React exhaustive-deps violation.
evidence: MapView.jsx:56-97 -- toast used at :77 and :91 but not in deps.
recommendedFix: Add toast to dependency array or add eslint-disable comment.

title: VendorList load failure silently shows empty table -- no error state or retry
detail: Lines 74-76: catch sets loading=false but no error surface. User sees empty table with no indication of failure.
evidence: VendorList.jsx:74-76 -- catch with no error state.
recommendedFix: Add error state and render above table with Retry button.

title: VendorList does not filter by dcfg_active_flag -- shows soft-deleted vendors
detail: Line 74: query has no active flag filter. Every other list screen filters active only. Inactive vendors appear in the list, inconsistent with the rest of the SPA.
evidence: VendorList.jsx:74 no active_flag filter, :288 renders both active and inactive states.
recommendedFix: Add `$filter=dcfg_active_flag eq true` or add an 'Include inactive' toggle.

title: VendorDetail renders null for missing vendor -- blank page with no guidance
detail: Line 88: `if (!vendor) return null;`. User sees nothing -- no back button, no error, no navigation. Should show a 'not found' message.
recommendedFix: Replace with a 'Vendor not found' message with back link, matching LocationDetail pattern.
